help.client_id: The name the program uses with BIMcloud when signing in. Leave it as it is.
help.destination: The folder where the backups are kept: a disk of this computer, an external disk or a network folder. To run with nobody signed in, use the \\server\folder path.
help.every: How often the backup runs by itself. In days, it runs at the time in “at”; in minutes and hours, it counts from midnight.
help.history: Each backup goes into a folder of its own. Folders older than this number of days are deleted, but at least the minimum number of backups is always kept.
help.latest: Each backup that finishes well replaces the previous one. It takes less space, but you cannot go back to an older version.
help.logged_off: For servers, where nobody stays signed in to Windows. When you save, the program asks for the password of your Windows account and hands it to the Task Scheduler; the program does not keep it. If you change the password, save again.
help.max_duration: If the backup takes longer than this, it stops and what was copied this time is discarded; the earlier backups are kept. 0 = no limit.
help.min_free_space: The backup stops if the destination disk has less free space than this, so the disk never fills up. 0 = do not check.
help.notify_failures: Shows a Windows notification when an automatic backup fails, finishes with errors, is cancelled or needs a new BIMcloud login.
help.projects_format: BIMProject is the full export of each project, made on the spot. PLN is the latest .pln BIMcloud itself saved: faster, but it may not have the latest changes. Both keeps the two.
help.snapshots: Snapshots are the backups BIMcloud keeps of each project and library. When checked, they go inside the exported file, which becomes much larger.
help.startup: When you sign in to Windows, the program opens by itself, with only the icon near the clock, to keep an eye on the backups.
help.username: The e-mail you sign in to BIMcloud with. If you fill it in, the login page already opens with it; it can be left blank.
help.verbose: Writes more details to the log, which helps to find a problem. The file gets larger.
